{{Short description|Norwegian-American author and mathematician}}
[[File:John Erik Fornaess.jpg|thumb|John Erik Fornæss]]
'''John Erik Fornæss''' (born 14 October 1946, [[Hamar, Norway]]) is a Norwegian-American mathematician and author. Fornæss earned his master's degree in 1970 from the [[University of Oslo]] with the thesis ''Uniform approximation on manifolds'' and earned his PhD in 1974 from the [[University of Washington]] under Edgar Lee Stout with thesis ''Embedding [[Function of several complex variables#Strongly (Strictly) pseudoconvex|Strictly Pseudoconvex]] Domains in Convex Domains''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=28253|title=John-Erik Fornæss}}</ref> At [[Princeton University]] in 1974, he became an instructor, assistant professor in 1976, associate professor in 1978, and a full professor in 1981. Since 1991, he has served as a professor at the [[University of Michigan]].

He concentrates on the geometry and dynamics of functions of various complex variables in his studies. He developed a Fatou-Julia theory in two complex variables with Nessim Sibony. Additionally, he is recognized for creating a counterexample in [[several complex variables]] in 1976.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Boas|first=Harold P.|date=2003|title=What is... a worm?|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/200305/what-is.pdf|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=50|pages=554–555}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fornaess|first1=John Erik|last2=Diederich|first2=Klas|date=1976|title=A strange bounded smooth domain of holomorphy|url=https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183537609|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|language=EN|volume=82|issue=1|pages=74–76|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1976-13964-X|issn=0002-9904|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Fornæss is a fellow of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27624|title=Gruppe 1: Matematiske fag|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]|language=no|access-date=24 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927170150/http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27624|archive-date=27 September 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2015, he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2016-04-27.</ref> Fornæss has an Erdős number of 2.
